::: {#thm-equivalent-cycle}
#### A cycle of conditionals

Let $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_k$ be propositions.
If $P_1 \Rightarrow P_2$, $P_2 \Rightarrow P_3$, $\ldots$, $P_{k-1} \Rightarrow P_k$ and $P_k \Rightarrow P_1$ are all true,
then $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ all have the same truth value.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Suppose one of the propositions, $P_i$, is true.
By modus ponens (@thm-inference-rules), $P_i \Rightarrow P_{i+1}$ makes $P_{i+1}$ true,
then $P_{i+1} \Rightarrow P_{i+2}$ makes $P_{i+2}$ true,
and so on around the cycle,
with $P_k \Rightarrow P_1$ leading from $P_k$ back to $P_1$,
until every proposition in the list is true.
So either all of $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ are true,
or none of them is true, and then all of them are false.

:::

:::
